question: A 47-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of urinary and fecal incontinence for 6 hours. Earlier in the day, he suffered a fall at a construction site and sustained injuries to his back and thighs but did not seek medical attention. He took ibuprofen for lower back pain. His temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F), pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 132/84 mm Hg. Examination shows tenderness over the lumbar spine, bilateral lower extremity weakness, absent ankle jerk reflexes, and preserved patellar reflexes. There is decreased rectal tone. An ultrasound of the bladder shows a full bladder. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Fall at construction site -> back and thigh injuries -> did not seek medical attention -> took ibuprofen for lower back pain -> urinary and fecal incontinence -> tenderness over lumbar spine -> bilateral lower extremity weakness -> absent ankle jerk reflexes -> preserved patellar reflexes -> decreased rectal tone -> full bladder on ultrasound -> Conus medullaris syndrome -> 95%
analysis: The patient's presentation with urinary and fecal incontinence, back and thigh injuries, lower extremity weakness, absent ankle jerk reflexes, preserved patellar reflexes, decreased rectal tone, and a full bladder on ultrasound is highly suggestive of conus medullaris syndrome. This syndrome involves damage to the conus medullaris, the end of the spinal cord, and can result in the described symptoms.
